newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ENGLAND BUILD BIG FIRST INNINGS LEAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND BUILD BIG FIRST INNINGS LEAD.

text.p: England tightened their grip on the first Ashes test against Australia on Friday, building a first innings lead of 331 runs on the second day at Edgbaston.
Only the weather can seemingly save the match for Australia, and the touring team's prayers were partly answered when play was stopped 80 minutes early due to rain.
England continued where they left off on Thursday, extending the overnight 200 for three to 449 for six in reply to Australia's paltry 118, thanks largely to a double century by Nasser Hussain.

Hussain, with an outstanding career-best score of 207, and Graham Thorpe (138) made it another miserable day for Australia, who are considering sending for at least one more bowler because of injuries to pacemen Jason Gillespie and Andy Bichel.
Just as worrying for them was the ineffectiveness of leg-spinner Shane Warne, whose one wicket in 35 overs cost 110 runs.
